question.text: A PMS portfolio holds 60% AAA corporate bonds and 40% AA+ corporate bonds. If the AAA-AA+ credit spread narrows, what happens to the portfolio?

answer.text: The AA+ bonds appreciate relative to AAA
The AAA bonds appreciate relative to AA+

explanation.text: The Logic: Credit-spread narrowing = AA+ yields drop toward AAA level = AA+ prices rise more than AAA. AA+ bonds outperform. The Trap: 'Both move up equally' misses the differential effect; spread compression helps the riskier bucket. Cross-Exam Context: IV and XV treat; XXI-B tests application. Manager's Pro-Tip: Playing credit-spread compression via a 'down-in-credit' rotation (buy BBB, sell AAA) is a classic late-cycle active trade — size cautiously.
